en: Writing materials, envelopes, office materials.

ex.en: He bought some stationery at the school store.
ex.ja: 彼は学校の売店で文房具を買った。

ex.en: I bought new notebooks and stationery to use at school.
ex.ja: 学校で使うノートや文房具を新しく買った。

ex.en: We buy stationery in bulk.
ex.ja: 私たちは文房具類を大量に買う。

note.ja: stationer（文房具屋）+ -y。stationer は大学の近くに店を構えた（stationary）書籍商から。stationary（静止した）と1字違い。

en: A topical substance formulated to protect the skin from the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation by absorbing, reflecting or scatteri…
To apply sunscreen to (someone).

ex.en: If you're going to the beach, you'll need sunscreen.
ex.ja: 海に行くんだったら、日焼け止めがいるね。

ex.en: If you're going to the beach, you need sunscreen.
ex.ja: 海に行くんだったら、日焼け止めがいるね。

ex.en: Ah, I forgot to apply sunscreen.
ex.ja: あ、日焼け止め塗ってくるの忘れた。

note.ja: sun（太陽）+ screen（遮るもの）。「日焼け止め」。

en: A storm, especially one with severe winds.
Any violent tumult or commotion.
To disturb, as by a tempest.

tempest.ety: From Old French tempeste (French tempête), from Latin tempestas (“storm”), from tempus (“time, weather”). Displaced native Old English hrīþ.

ex.en: Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law are a tempest and hailstorm.
ex.ja: 嫁と姑の仲は大嵐。

note.ja: ラテン語 tempestas（天候・嵐）から。tempus（時）の仲間。荒れた天候 →「大嵐・大騒ぎ」。

en: A protein-rich food made from curdled soy milk.
A box or rectangle, empty or with a question mark or hexadecimal code inside, displayed by some systems in place of a character not suppo…

tofu.ety: Borrowed from Japanese 豆(とう)腐(ふ) (tōfu), from Middle Chinese 豆腐 (duwᴴ bju^X, “curdled bean”). Doublet of dubu and doufu.

ex.en: Please buy some tofu on your way home.
ex.ja: 帰る途中に豆腐を買ってきてください。

ex.en: Buy some tofu on your way home.
ex.ja: 帰る途中でお豆腐買ってきてよ。

ex.en: Get some tofu on the way back.
ex.ja: 帰る途中でお豆腐買ってきてよ。

note.ja: 日本語「豆腐」から。中国語にさかのぼる。

en: A bandage and belt used to hold a hernia in place.
A structure made up of one or more triangular units made from straight beams of wood or metal, which is used to support a structure as in…
To tie up a bird before cooking it.
To secure or bind with ropes.

truss.ety: From Middle English trusse, from Old French trousse, torse, from Vulgar Latin *torsus, variant of Classical Latin tortus, past participle of torqueō. Doublet of torse and trousse.

ex.en: The girls were trussed up and left in a cellar.
ex.ja: 少女たちは縛り上げられて地下室に放置された。

ex.en: He trussed up the thief.
ex.ja: 彼はその泥棒を縛り上げた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 trousser（束ねる）から。「縛る」→「トラス（骨組み）」。trousers と同系とされる。

Which ought not to be done; illegal; unjustified.

en: Firm; unshakeable; unyielding; determined.
Very difficult to break, pierce, or cut.
An unspecified mineral or rock of virtually impenetrable hardness.
In later use: diamond.

adamant.ety: From Middle English adamant, adamaunt, from Latin adamantem, accusative singular form of adamās (“hard as steel”), from Ancient Greek ἀδάμαντ- (adámant-, “invincible”), oblique stem of ἀδάμας (adámas). Doublet of diamond.

ex.en: I'm adamant that you should go.
ex.ja: 君に行ってもらわねば承知しない。

ex.en: Bill was adamant that she should obey him.
ex.ja: ビルは絶対に彼女が彼に従うべきだと譲らなかった。

ex.en: I am adamant that he undertake it.
ex.ja: 彼が引き受けるべきだという私の考えは不動だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 adamas（征服できない・最も硬い石）から。「断固とした」。diamond も同じ語源。

en: A specified portion of the atmosphere, especially that under the technical aviation control and/or jurisdiction of a particular state ove…
That part of the sky designated for the sole use of aircraft.

ex.en: The Air Force has the control of the airspace.
ex.ja: 空軍が制空権を握っている。

ex.en: A commercial airplane allegedly violated military airspace.
ex.ja: 民間機が軍事的領域を侵犯したとのことです。

note.ja: air（空）+ space（空間）。「領空」。

en: To distribute or apportion by (or as if by) lot.
To assign or designate as a task or for a purpose.

allot.ety: From Middle English allotten, from Old French aloter (Modern French allotir). à + lot. By surface analysis, al- + lot.

ex.en: Tickets will be allotted in order of application.
ex.ja: 切符は、申し込み順に割り当てます。

ex.en: They allotted to each player the benefits due him.
ex.ja: 彼らは各選手に支払われるべき利益を分配した。

ex.en: Each speaker was allotted five minutes.
ex.ja: 各人五分ずつ話す時間が与えられた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 aloter（くじで分ける）から。a + lot（くじ）。「割り当てる」。

en: Full of ardor; expressing passion, spirit, or enthusiasm.
Providing light or heat.

ardent.ety: First attested circa 14th century as Middle English ardaunt, borrowed from Anglo-Norman ardent and Old French ardant, from Latin ardentem, accusative of ardēns, present participle of ardeō (“to burn”).

ex.en: He went abroad in opposition to her ardent wishes.
ex.ja: 彼女の熱心な希望に逆らって彼は外国へ行った。

ex.en: It is our ardent hope that the war will end soon.
ex.ja: 戦争の早期終結が我々の熱烈な願いです。

ex.en: He yielded to her ardent wishes.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女の熱烈な願いに負けた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ardere（燃える）の現在分詞。「燃えるような」→「熱烈な」。arson と同じ。

en: A racquet sport played indoors on a court by two opposing players (singles) or two opposing pairs of players (doubles), in which a shuttl…
A cooling summer drink made with claret, sugar, and soda water.

badminton.ety: Named after Badminton House, an estate in Gloucestershire owned by the Duke of Beaufort, where the game was first played in England. For the house name, see Badminton.

ex.en: What's the difference between badminton and tennis?
ex.ja: バトミントンとテニスはどう違うの？

ex.en: Playing badminton is a lot of fun.
ex.ja: バドミントンって、すごく楽しいね。

ex.en: I used to play badminton, but I don't anymore.
ex.ja: 私は以前はバトミントンをやったものですが、今はもうやりません。

note.ja: この遊びが流行したイギリスのボーフォート公爵の邸宅バドミントン・ハウスから。

en: The solid rock found at some depth below the ground surface.
A basis or foundation.
To establish on a solid foundation.

bedrock.ety: From bed (“a layer on top of which something else rests.”) + rock.

ex.en: Love is the bedrock of my life.
ex.ja: 愛を基盤に生きている。

note.ja: bed（下地）+ rock（岩）。「岩盤」→「基盤」。

en: A slightly elevated path (walkway) for pedestrians over sandy or swampy ground, typically made out of wood; specifically (Canada, US) one…
To install a boardwalk over.

ex.en: The city is planning to extend the boardwalk.
ex.ja: 市は遊歩道を拡張する計画だ。

note.ja: board（板）+ walk（歩道）。「板張りの遊歩道」。

en: In a bold manner; with confidence.

boldly.ety: From Middle English boldely, boldeliche, baldeliche, from Old English bealdlīċe (“boldly, earnestly”), equivalent to bold + -ly.

ex.en: She boldly went up to the king.
ex.ja: 彼女は臆することなく王の面前に出た。

ex.en: I was about to reply, when he boldly cut in.
ex.ja: 私が返事をしようとした矢先に、彼が口を出してきた。

ex.en: I boldly painted my answer.
ex.ja: 私は自分の答えを大胆に描きました。

note.ja: bold（大胆な）+ -ly。「大胆に」。

en: Inflexible; liable to break, snap, or shatter easily under stress, pressure, or impact.
Not physically tough or tenacious; apt to break or crumble when bending.
A confection of caramelized sugar and nuts.
Anything resembling this confection, such as flapjack, a cereal bar, etc.
To become brittle.

brittle.ety: From Middle English britel, brutel, brotel (“brittle”), from Old English *brytel, *bryttol (“brittle, fragile”, literally “prone to or tending to break”); equivalent to brit + -le.

ex.en: Metals can become brittle at low temperatures.
ex.ja: 金属は低温になると脆くなることがあります。

note.ja: 古英語 brēotan（壊す）から。「もろい」。

en: Someone or something that climbs (such as a mountain climber).
A plant such as a vine that climbs upwards as it grows by attaching itself to some support.

climber.ety: From Middle English clymbere, clymber (“one who climbs, climber”), from climben (“to climb; to ascend, fly upward, rise; to slope upwards; to approach God in prayer; to advance; to overcome, triumph; to aspire; to be presumptuous”) + -er, -ere (suffix forming agent nouns). The English word is analysable as climb (verb) + -er (suffix forming agent nouns).

ex.en: He is a fine type of mountain climber.
ex.ja: 彼は登山家の良い見本だ。

ex.en: Falling rocks present a danger to climbers.
ex.ja: 落石は登山者にとって危険である。

ex.en: The climbers were brought off by the rescue party.
ex.ja: 登山者たちは救助隊に救助された。

en: Having an obstructed flow; blocked.

ex.en: The street is clogged with traffic.
ex.ja: 通りは車で交通が渋滞している。

ex.en: The machine was clogged with grease.
ex.ja: 機械はグリースで動きが悪くなった。

ex.en: My throat feels clogged up.
ex.ja: のどが詰まった感じです。

To force, constrain, or coerce.

en: A pipe or channel for conveying water, etc.
A duct or tube into which electrical cables may be pulled: electrical conduit.

conduit.ety: From Middle English conduyt, condit, from Old French conduit, from Latin conductus. Doublet of conduct.

Anything that conveys, transports or delivers.

note.ja: convey（運ぶ）+ -or。con + via（道）。「コンベヤー」。

en: Uncomfortably restricted in size or space, or financially.
Overcrowded or congested.

ex.en: My house is small and cramped.
ex.ja: 私のうちは小さくて、狭いです。

ex.en: This room is cramped.
ex.ja: この部屋は狭苦しい。

ex.en: Train compartments soon get cramped.
ex.ja: 列車のコンパートメントはすぐ窮屈になる。

en: Of a heavenly body, to be at the highest point, reach its greatest altitude.
To reach the (physical or figurative) summit, highest point, peak etc.
Relating to the culmen.
Growing upward, as opposed to lateral growth.

culminate.ety: First attested in 1647; borrowed from Medieval Latin culminātus, perfect passive participle of culminō (“to crown”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from Latin culmen (“peak, highest point”, oblique stem culmin-) + -ō (verb-forming suffix), older form columen (“top, summit”), from Proto-Italic *kolamen, from a Proto-Indo-European base *kol-, *kelH- (“to project, rise; peak, summit, top”), whence also English hill and holm.

ex.en: All her efforts culminated in failure.
ex.ja: 彼女のすべての努力は水泡に帰した。

ex.en: His career culminated in the presidency.
ex.ja: 彼は出世して最後には大統領になった。

en: Concerning numbers expressed in decimal or mathematical calculations performed using decimal.
A number expressed in the base-ten system, (particularly) a fractional numeral written in this system.
The decimal system itself.
To represent with numbers after a decimal point.

decimal.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin, Medieval Latin decimalis, from Latin decimus, from decem (“ten”) + adjective suffix -alis.

ex.en: In 1971 the United Kingdom changed its currency to the decimal system.
ex.ja: 英国は、１９７１年にその貨幣制度を１０進法に移行させた。

ex.en: This is a decimal number.
ex.ja: これは十進数表記です。

ex.en: Convert the following fractions to decimals.
ex.ja: 次の分数を小数に直しなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 decimus（10番目の）から。decem（10）。「十進法の・小数」。December（もと10番目の月）と同じ。

No longer in business or service, nor expected to be again; out of business.
To make defunct.
The dead person (referred to).

defunct.ety: Borrowed from Latin dēfunctus, past participle of dēfungor (“to finish, discharge”).

en: To lower in value or social position.
To reduce in quality or purity.

ex.en: Don't degrade yourself by telling such a lie.
ex.ja: そんなうそをついて自分の値打ちをさげるな。

ex.en: He degraded himself by telling me lies.
ex.ja: 僕に嘘をつくとは彼も落ちたもんだ。

ex.en: Drug addiction degraded many people.
ex.ja: 麻薬中毒で多くの人が堕落した。

en: To spread (something) over or through as in air, water, or other matter, especially by fluid motion or passive means.
To be spread over or through as in air, water, or other matter, especially by fluid motion or passive means.
Everywhere or throughout everything; not focused or concentrated.
Wordy; verbose.

diffuse.ety: From Middle French diffuser, from Latin diffūsus, past participle of diffundere, from dis- + fundere.

ex.en: A great light was diffused over the baseball stadium.
ex.ja: 凄い明かりが野球場にあたっていた。

ex.en: The lotus blossoms diffused an inexpressibly pleasant scent.
ex.ja: 蓮の花はなんとも言えない芳香をはなっていた。

note.ja: dif（ばらばらに）+ fus（注ぐ）+ e。注いで広げる →「拡散させる・散漫な」。

ex.en: You look very dignified.
ex.ja: 貫禄がついたね。

note.ja: dignify（威厳を与える）+ -ed。ラテン語 dignus（ふさわしい）。「威厳のある」。dignity と同じ。

ex.ja: 露骨に嫌な顔をして、彼を睨みつけた。

ex.en: He couldn't suffer the slightest disobedience in his men.
ex.ja: 部下の不服従はどんなに小さなものでも我慢できなかった。

ex.en: I was condemned for my disobedience.
ex.ja: 不服従でとがめられた。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ obedience（服従）。「不服従」。

en: One who dreams.
Someone whose beliefs are far from realistic.

dreamer.ety: From Middle English dremer, dremere, dremare, equivalent to dream + -er. Cognate with West Frisian dreamer (“dreamer”), Saterland Frisian Dröömer (“dreamer”), Dutch dromer (“dreamer”), German Träumer (“dreamer”), Danish drømmer (“dreamer”), Swedish drömmare (“dreamer”).

ex.en: He is nothing more than a dreamer.
ex.ja: 彼は夢想家にすぎない。

ex.en: She is, in a word, a dreamer.
ex.ja: 彼女は一言でいえば夢想家だ。

ex.en: He is no more than a dreamer.
ex.ja: 彼は空想家にすぎない。

note.ja: dream（夢見る）+ -er。「夢見る人」。

en: Actual or threatened force for the purpose of compelling action by another person; the act of coercing.
Use of physical or moral force to compel a person to do something, or to abstain from doing something, thereby depriving that person of t…

coercion.ety: Inherited from Middle English cohercioun, from Old French cohercion, from Latin coërcitiō (“magisterial coercion”), from past participle coercitus of coërceō (“to restrain, coerce”), from co- (“with”) + arceō (“to shut in, enclose”); see coerce.

ex.en: Leadership by coercion would not produce the results we see.
ex.ja: 脅しによるリーダーシップは、いまぼくたちが目にするような結果を生み出しはしない。

ex.en: Certainly there are downsides to leadership by coercion and force.
ex.ja: 力と脅しによるリーダーシップには確かにマイナス面があることは確かだ。

note.ja: coerce（強制する）+ -ion。co + arcere（閉じ込める）。「強制」。

en: The punctuation mark ⟨,⟩ used to indicate a set of parts of a sentence or between elements of a list.
A similar-looking subscript diacritical mark.

comma.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)kep-?
Proto-Hellenic *kopt͏̌ō
Ancient Greek κόπτω (kóptō)
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥
Proto-Hellenic *-mə
Ancient Greek -μᾰ (-mă)
Ancient Greek κόμμα (kómma)
Latin commabor.
English comma
From Latin comma, from Ancient Greek κόμμα (kómma), from κόπτω (kóptō, “to cut”).

ex.en: I suggest putting a comma here.
ex.ja: ここにカンマを入れるといいですよ。

ex.en: In another paragraph, he put in a comma.
ex.ja: 別の段落で彼はコンマを１つ入れた。

ex.en: Don't run on your sentences with commas.
ex.ja: コンマで文を次々につないではいけない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 komma（切られたもの・文の区切り）から。koptein（切る）。「コンマ」。

en: The ability to perform some task; competence.
An individual's capacity to understand the nature and implications of their legal rights and obligations.

competency.ety: From Late Latin competentia. Doublet of competence.

note.ja: competent（有能な）+ -cy。「能力・適性」。

en: The ventral area (very bottom) of the human body between where the legs fork from the torso, in the area of the genitals and anus.
The area where something forks or branches: where a ramification takes place.
To provide with a crotch; to give the form of a crotch to.
To notch (a log) on opposite sides to provide a grip for the dogs that will haul it.

crotch.ety:
Of disputed origin; two possibilities seem likely:
* From Middle English croche, variant of crucche (“crutch”); compare crook.
* From Middle English croche, variant of crouche (“cross, crozier”).

ex.en: Doctor, I've got an itch in my crotch.
ex.ja: 先生、アソコがかゆいんです。

ex.en: I have an itchy crotch.
ex.ja: 局部にかゆみがあります。

ex.en: My crotch hurts from riding the bicycle too much.
ex.ja: 自転車の乗り過ぎで股が痛いです。

note.ja: crutch（松葉づえ：二股の棒）の変化形とされる。「股」。

en: that has been subject to crucifixion

ex.en: The two lovers who eloped were crucified.
ex.ja: 駆け落ちをした二人は磔になってしまったんです。

en: Of or relating to a department.

departmental.ety: Borrowed from French départemental. By surface analysis, department + -al. Doublet of départemental.

note.ja: de + part（分ける）+ ment + al。部門（department）の →「部門の・学科の」。

en: To put down; to lay down; to deposit; to lay aside; to put away.
To remove (a leader) from (high) office without killing (them).

depose.ety: Recorded since c.1300, from Middle English, from Old French deposer, from de- (“down”) + poser (“to put, place”). Deposition (1494 in the legal sense) belongs to deposit, but that related word and depose became thoroughly confused.

en: The natural order of the universe; natural law, cosmic order.
One's obligation in respect to one's position in society, or the universe; one's duty, societally or cosmically.

dharma.ety: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit धर्म (dhárma, “that which upholds or supports”). The definitions pertaining to Buddhism are influenced by dhamma, a loan word from Pali. Doublet of dhamma and firm.

note.ja: サンスクリット語 dharma（法・掟）から。「保つもの」が原義。

en: A method of separating molecules or particles of different sizes by differential diffusion through a semipermeable membrane.
The use of this method for the removal of waste products from the blood in the case of kidney failure: hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.

dialysis.ety: From Latin dialysis, from Ancient Greek διάλυσις (diálusis). By surface analysis, dia- + -lysis. First use appears c. 1550.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dialysis（分離）から。dia + lyein（ほどく）。「（血液を）分けてきれいにすること」→「透析」。analysis と同じ。

en: An authoritative principle, belief or statement of opinion, especially one considered to be absolutely true and indisputable, regardless …
A doctrine (or set of doctrines) relating to matters such as morality and faith, set forth authoritatively by a religious organization or…

dogma.ety: From Latin dogma (“philosophical tenet”), from Ancient Greek δόγμα (dógma, “opinion, tenet”), from δοκέω (dokéō, “to seem good, think”). Treated in the 17th and 18th century as Greek, with plural dogmata. Compare decent.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dogma（意見・決定）から。dokein（思われる）。「教義」→「独断的な考え」。orthodox の doxa と同系。

en: The state or feeling of being empty; an emotion that combines hollowness, numbness, disconnection and a lack of meaning in life, resultin…
A void; a nothingness; something lacking existence.

emptiness.ety: Inherited from Middle English emptynesse, from Old English ǣmtiġnes. By surface analysis, empty + -ness.

ex.en: I feel an overbearing emptiness inside of me.
ex.ja: 自分が空っぽすぎて辛い。

ex.en: Form is emptiness, emptiness is form.
ex.ja: 色即是空、空即是色。

note.ja: empty（空の）+ -ness。「空虚」。

en: A badge of office, rank, or power.
The lowest grade of commissioned officer in the United States Navy, junior to a lieutenant junior grade.
To distinguish by a mark or ornament.
To distinguish by an ornament, especially by a crown.

ensign.ety: From Middle English ensigne, from Old French enseigne, from Latin īnsignia, nominative plural of īnsigne, meaning marked, distinguished. Doublet of insignia.

note.ja: en（中に）+ sign（印）。印の入った旗 →「軍旗・（米海軍の）少尉」。

en: To call out; to draw out or bring forth.
To cause the manifestation of something (emotion, picture, etc.) in someone's mind or imagination.

evoke.ety: From French évoquer, from Latin ēvocō (“to call out, summon”), from ex (“out”) and vocō (“call”). Akin to voice.

ex.en: The music evokes memories of an earlier time.
ex.ja: その音楽を聞くと昔のことを思い出す。

ex.en: This cuisine is seasoned to evoke the esprit of Paris.
ex.ja: このお料理は、パリのエスプリを意識して、味付けしてみました。

note.ja: ラテン語 evocare（呼び出す）から。e + vocare（呼ぶ）。「呼び起こす」。voice と同じ voc。

en: In a faithful manner.
A conventional formula for ending a letter, used when the salutation addresses the person for whom the letter is intended using an honori…

faithfully.ety: From Middle English feithfulli, equivalent to faithful + -ly.

ex.en: Take this medicine faithfully, and you will feel better.
ex.ja: この薬を正確に飲みなさい。そうすれば気分がよくなるでしょう。

ex.en: He carried out the scheme faithfully.
ex.ja: 彼はその計画を忠実に実行した。

ex.en: He performed his duties faithfully.
ex.ja: 彼は職務を忠実に実行した。

en: Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce b…
A light green color inspired by the color of ferns.

fern.ety:
From Middle English fern, from Old English fearn, from Proto-West Germanic *farn, from Proto-Germanic *farnaz (“fern”), from Proto-Indo-European *pornóm (“feather, wing; fern, leaf”), from *p(t)erH- (“fern”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots fairn (“fern”), North Frisian farne (“fern”), West Frisian fear (“fern”), Dutch varen (“fern”), German Farn, Farm (“fern”), Luxembourgish Far (“fern”); also Breton raden (“fern”), Cornish reden (“ferns; brackens”), Welsh rhedyn (“ferns; brackens”), Latvian paparde (“fern; bracken”), spārns (“wing”), Lithuanian spar̃nas (“wing”), Bulgarian and Macedonian папрат

note.ja: 古英語 fearn（シダ）から。「シダ」。

en: The tip of the human finger.
To move or deflect with the fingertips.

fingertip.ety: From finger + tip. Compare tiptoe and toetip.

ex.en: He has the subject at his fingertips.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題に精通している。

ex.en: He blew on his fingertips.
ex.ja: 彼は指先に息を吹きかけた。

ex.en: I burned my fingertip.
ex.ja: 私は指先を火傷した。

note.ja: finger（指）+ tip（先）。「指先」→ at one's fingertips（すぐ使える）。

en: The capacity of a weapon to deliver fire onto a target.
The ability to deliver fire.

note.ja: fire（火）+ power（力）。「火力」。

en: The act of fixing.
The state of being fixed or fixated.

fixation.ety: From Old French fixation. By surface analysis, fix + -ation.

note.ja: fix（固定する）+ -ation。ラテン語 figere（固定する）。「固定・執着」。

ja: 形成の（formative years：人格形成期）

en: Capable of forming something.
Capable of producing new tissue.
A thing which causes formation to occur.
A language unit, typically a morph, that has a morphological function (that is, forming a word from a root or another word).

formative.ety: From Middle English formatyve, formatif (“having the ability to form”), from Old French formatif, formative (modern French formatif), from Medieval Latin formātīvus, from Latin fōrmātus + -īvus (suffix forming adjectives with the sense ‘doing’ or ‘related to doing’). Fōrmātus is the perfect passive participle of fōrmō (“to form, to shape”), from fōrma (“a form, shape”); further etymology uncertain, possibly related to Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ, “a form, shape”) (see further at that entry). By surface analysis, form + -ative.

en: To chafe or irritate; to worry.
To make rough, to agitate or disturb; to cause to ripple.
Agitation of the surface of a fluid by fermentation or some other cause; a rippling on the surface of water.
Agitation of the mind marked by complaint and impatience; disturbance of temper; irritation.

fret.ety:
From Middle English frēten (“to eat (at), corrode, destroy, annoy”), from Old English fretan (“to eat up, devour; to fret; to break, burst”), from Proto-West Germanic *fraetan, from Proto-Germanic *fraetaną (“to consume, devour, eat up”), from Proto-Germanic *fra- (“for-, prefix meaning ‘completely, fully’”) (from Proto-Indo-European *pro- (“forward, toward”)) + *etaną (“to eat”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ed- (“to eat”)).
The senses meaning “to chafe, rub” could also be due to sound-association with Anglo-Norman *freiter (modern dialectal French fretter), from Vulgar Latin *frict

ex.en: That child is always fretting.
ex.ja: あの子はいつもだだをこねている。

ex.en: You need not fret over such trifles.
ex.ja: そんなささいなことでクヨクヨするな。

ex.en: Don’t fret about it. Nobody can do it perfectly from the start.
ex.ja: 焦っちゃだめだよ。最初から完璧にできる人なんていないんだから。

note.ja: 「くよくよする」は古英語 fretan（食い尽くす）から。ギターの fret は別語。

en: Of or pertaining to the stomach and intestines, and thus to digestion.

gastrointestinal.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gres-der.
Ancient Greek γρᾰ́ω (grắō)
Proto-Indo-European *-tḗr
Proto-Hellenic *-tḗr
Ancient Greek -τήρ (-tḗr)
Ancient Greek γᾰστήρ (găstḗr)der.
English gastro-
English intestinal
English gastrointestinal
From gastro- + intestinal.

en: The act of gratifying or pleasing, either the mind, or the appetite or taste.
A gratuity; a reward.

gratification.ety: From Latin grātificātiō either directly or through Middle French gratification, from Latin grātificō (“to do a favor to, oblige, please, gratify”), from grātus (“kind, pleasing”) + faciō (“to make”).

ex.en: That job gave him little gratification.
ex.ja: その仕事をしても彼はほとんど満足感が得られなかった。

ex.en: He had the gratification of seeing his son graduate from collage.
ex.ja: 彼は息子の大学卒業の喜びに浸っていた。

note.ja: grat（喜ばしい）+ i + fic（する）+ ation。喜ばせること →「満足（感）・欲求の充足」。

en: Repellently frightful and shocking; ghastly, horrific.
Awful, terrible.

gruesome.ety:
From grue (“(archaic except Northern England, Scotland) to be frightened; to shudder with fear”) + -some (suffix meaning ‘characterized by some specific condition or quality, usually to a considerable degree’ forming adjectives and nouns), probably popularized by the Scottish novelist and poet Walter Scott (1771–1832): see, for example, the 1816 quotation.
cognates
* Danish grusom (“cruel; horrible”)
* Middle Dutch grousaem, grusaem (modern Dutch gruwzaam (“cruel; gruesome”))
* Middle High German grûsam, grûwesam (modern German grausam (“cruel”))
* Norwegian Bokmål grusom (“cruel; horrible”)

note.ja: grue（身震いする）+ -some。「ぞっとする」。

en: In a harsh manner; severely.

harshly.ety:
Etymology tree
English harsh
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English harshly
From harsh + -ly.

ex.en: I wonder why Mary always talks that harshly.
ex.ja: メアリーって、何でああもトゲのある言い方するんだろうね？

ex.en: He spoke yet more harshly.
ex.ja: 彼はさらにいっそう激しい口調で語った。

ex.en: I really spoke too harshly.
ex.ja: ちょっと言い過ぎました。

note.ja: harsh（厳しい）+ -ly。「厳しく」。

en: A catastrophe.

Hiroshima.ety: Borrowed from Japanese 広(ひろ)島(しま) (Hiroshima). Transliteration of Japanese ひろしま

ex.en: She likes Hiroshima better than any other city.
ex.ja: 彼女は他のどの都市よりも広島が好きだ。

ex.en: I go to Hiroshima three times a month.
ex.ja: 私は月に３回広島へ行きます。

ex.en: I never went to Hiroshima on my trip.
ex.ja: 広島へは一度も行ったことがないです。

en: Combined chemically with water.
Not suffering from dehydration.
Able to be imagined; conceivable.
Within the realm of consideration.

imaginable.ety: From Middle English ymaginable, from Latin imāginābilis; equivalent to imagine + -able.

ex.en: This is the best play imaginable.
ex.ja: これは考えられる最高の劇だ。

ex.en: I have tried every means imaginable.
ex.ja: 考えられる限りの、あらゆる手段を試みた。

ex.en: I've tried every means imaginable.
ex.ja: 考えられる限りの、あらゆる手段を試みた。

note.ja: imagine（想像する）+ -able。「想像できる」。

en: Anything that impels; a stimulating factor.
A force, either internal or external, that impels; an impulse.

impetus.ety: Borrowed from Latin impetus (“a rushing upon, an attack, assault, onset”), from impetō (“to rush upon, attack”), from in- (“upon”) + petō (“to seek, fall upon”).

note.ja: ラテン語 impetus（突進・攻撃）から。in + petere（向かう）。「勢い・はずみ」。compete と同じ pet。

en: Having the power of driving or impelling; giving an impulse; moving; impellent.
Actuated by impulse or by transient feelings; inclined to make rapid decisions without due consideration.
That which impels or gives an impulse; an impelling agent.
One whose behaviour or personality is characterized by being impulsive.

impulsive.ety: Borrowed from Middle French impulsif, from Latin impulsivus.

note.ja: im（中から）+ puls（押す）+ ive。衝動（impulse）に押される →「衝動的な」。

en: Biotic material that releases fragrant smoke when burnt, often used in religious rites or for aesthetic reasons.
The fragrant smoke released by burning incense (sense 1).
To anger; to infuriate.
To offer incense to.

incense.ety: From Middle English encens, from Old French encens (“sweet-smelling substance”) from Late Latin incensum (“burnt incense”, literally “something burnt”), neuter past participle of incendō (“to set on fire”). Compare incendiary. Doublet of incienso. Displaced native Old English rēcels.

ex.en: She was somehow incensed against me.
ex.ja: どういうわけか、彼女は僕にひどく怒っていた。

ex.en: He was incensed by their lack of incentives.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らのやる気の無さに激怒した。

note.ja: ラテン語 incendere（燃やす）から。「燃やす香」→「香」、心を燃やす →「激怒させる」。incendiary と同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to inhumanity and the indifferently cruel, sadistic or barbaric behavior it brings.
Transcending or different than what is human.

inhuman.ety: From Middle English inhumayne, from Middle French inhumain and its etymon Latin inhūmānus.

note.ja: in（否定）+ human（人間の）。「非人間的な」。

en: A bill; a commercial document issued by a seller to a buyer indicating the products, quantities and agreed prices for products or service…
The lot or set of goods as shipped or received.
To bill; to issue an invoice to.
To make an invoice for (goods or services).

invoice.ety: Borrowed from Middle French envois pl, plural of envoi, from the verb envoyer (“to send”). See also envoy.

ex.en: Our records show that the invoice No.1111 is still outstanding.
ex.ja: 請求書１１１１は未払いになっております。

ex.en: This whole thing is the invoice.
ex.ja: これ全部、請求書。

ex.en: Is this all the invoices.
ex.ja: これって、全部請求書？

note.ja: 古い複数形 invoyes（送られたもの）から。フランス語 envoyer（送る）。「送り状・請求書」。envoy と同じ。

en: A Tai ethnic group native to Southeast Asia.
The official language of Laos that is closely related to Thai.
Of, from, or pertaining to Laos, the Lao people or their Kra-Dai Lao language.

ex.en: Vientiane is the capital of Laos.
ex.ja: ヴィエンチャンはラオスの首都。

note.ja: ラオスの民族名・言語名。Laos と同じ。

en: Existing or present, but concealed or inactive.
Remaining in an inactive or hidden phase; dormant.
The residue left by a person's finger that can be made visible by a process such as powder dusting; a latent fingerprint.
An underlying cause that can be inferred from statistical correlations; factor.

latent.ety: From Middle English latent, latente, from Old French latent, from Latin latēns, present participle of lateō (“lie hidden”).

note.ja: ラテン語 latere（隠れている）の現在分詞。「潜在的な」。latency と同じ。

en: Without limits in extent, size, or quantity.

limitless.ety:
Etymology tree
English limit
Proto-Indo-European *lewh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *lewHs-der.
Proto-Germanic *leusaną
Proto-Germanic *lausaz
Proto-Germanic *-lausaz
Proto-West Germanic *-laus
Old English -lēas
Middle English -les
English -less
English limitless
From limit + -less.

ex.en: Natural resources are not limitless.
ex.ja: 天然資源は無限に存在するわけではない。

ex.en: We have used earth's energy resources as if they were limitless.
ex.ja: 私達は、地球のエネルギー資源をまるで無尽蔵であるかのように使ってきた。

note.ja: limit（限界）+ -less。「無限の」。

en: Able to read and write; having literacy.
Knowledgeable in literature, writing; literary; well-read.
A person who is able to read and write.
A person who was educated but had not taken a university degree; especially a candidate to take holy orders.

literate.ety:
Inherited from Middle English litterate, borrowed from Latin lītterātus, līterātus, see -ate (adjective-forming suffix) and -ate (noun-forming suffix). Doublet of literato and literatus.
Displaced native Old English stæfwīs.

note.ja: ラテン語 litteratus（文字を知った）から。littera（文字）。「読み書きのできる」。letter、literature と同じ。

ja: ローカライゼーション

en: The act of localizing.
The switch of positions in power from the colonizing population to the local population.

note.ja: loc（場所）+ alization。ある場所に合わせること →「現地化・局在化」。

en: Not high; not elevated in place; low.
Low in rank or social importance.
In a low manner; humbly; meekly; modestly.
In a low condition; meanly.

lowly.ety: From low + -ly; compare Middle English lowly.

en: Clear; easily understood.
Mentally rational; sane.
A lucid dream.

lucid.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *lewk-
Proto-Indo-European *-yeti
Proto-Indo-European *-éyeti
Proto-Indo-European *lowkéyeti
Proto-Italic *loukeō
Proto-Indo-European *lewk-
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₁ti
Proto-Indo-European *-yeti
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₁yeti
Proto-Indo-European *lukéh₁yeti
Proto-Italic *l(o)ukēō?
Latin lūceō
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der.
Proto-Italic *-iðos
Latin -idus
Latin lūcidus
English lucid
Latin lucidus, from lūceō (“shine”) + -idus.

en: A malignant tumor that arises in the lymph nodes or in other lymphoid tissue.

lymphoma.ety: From lymph, from Latin lympha (“water”) + -oma (“disease, morbidity”).

note.ja: lymph（リンパ）+ -oma（腫瘍）。「リンパ腫」。

en: A cocktail made with gin or vodka and vermouth.
Any cocktail served in a cocktail glass, often sweet or fruity and aimed at women.

ex.en: A vodka martini, please.
ex.ja: ウォッカマティーニをお願いします。

note.ja: イタリアのベルモットのブランド名 Martini から。

en: Showing mercy.

merciful.ety: From Middle English merciful, mercyful, equivalent to mercy + -ful. Displaced native Old English mildheort.

ex.en: In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful.
ex.ja: 慈悲深く慈悲あまねき神の御名において。

note.ja: mercy（慈悲）+ -ful。「慈悲深い」。mercy はラテン語 merces（報酬）。

en: A person, usually a woman, who is trained to assist women in childbirth, but who is not a physician.
To act as a midwife.
To facilitate the emergence of.

midwife.ety: From Middle English midwif, corresponding to mid (“with”) + wif (“woman, wife, female”). It appears not to be entirely clear whether the original understanding was “with-woman” in the sense of “attending/assisting woman”, or “they who are with the woman” (namely the mother).

ex.en: Mary is studying to become a midwife.
ex.ja: メアリーは助産婦を目指して勉強しています。

ex.en: Mary is a midwife.
ex.ja: メアリーは助産師です。

note.ja: mid（〜と共に）+ wife（女性）。「（産婦と）共にいる女性」→「助産師」。

en: Information that is incorrect, whether intentionally or unintentionally.

misinformation.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *mey-?
Proto-Indo-European *meyth₂-der.
Proto-Germanic *missaz
Proto-Germanic *missa-
Proto-West Germanic *missa-
Old English mis-
Middle English mys-
English mis-
Proto-Indo-European *h₁én
Proto-Italic *en
Proto-Italic *en-
Latin in-
Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ)der.?
Latin fōrma
Latin fōrmō
Latin īnfōrmō
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Late Latin īnfōrmātiōder.
Middle English enformacioun
English information
English misinformation
From mis- + information.

ex.en: Don't let the misinformation spreading jerk speak.
ex.ja: デマ野郎にしゃべらせるな。

note.ja: mis（誤って）+ in + form（形）+ ation。誤った情報 →「誤情報」。

en: The act of mobilizing.
The marshalling and organizing of troops and national resources in preparation for war, bringing them to a state of readiness for an action.

note.ja: mob（動く）+ ilization。動員できるようにすること →「動員・結集」。

en: A long speech by one person in a play; sometimes a soliloquy; other times spoken to other characters.
A long series of comic stories and jokes as an entertainment.
To speak in or deliver a monologue.

monoxide.ety: Formed as mon- + oxide; compare the earlier dioxide, pentoxide, and tetroxide.

en: In a musical manner.
In terms of music.

musically.ety: From Middle English musicallye, musikili; equivalent to musical + -ly.

ex.ja: トムには音楽の才能もある。

ex.ja: トムには音楽の才能もある。

en: An organized rebellion against a legally constituted authority, especially by seamen against their officers.
Violent commotion; tumult; strife.
To commit a mutiny.

note.ja: ラテン語 movere（動かす）から古フランス語 mutin（反抗的な）を経た語。→「反乱（特に船上・軍隊）」。※ mut（変える）とは別系統。

en: Persistently annoying or painful.
The action of the verb nag.

ex.en: My wife's constant nagging is getting me down.
ex.ja: 妻に四六時中ぶつぶつ言われるのには憂鬱になってしまう。

ex.en: Mike is always nagging his father to buy him a car.
ex.ja: マイクはしょっちゅう父親に車を買ってくれとせがんでいる。

ex.en: My wife's constant nagging really gets on my nerves.
ex.ja: 妻のひっきりなしの愚痴話には本当にいらいらする。

note.ja: nervous（神経質な）+ -ly。「びくびくして」。

en: The hours of darkness between sunset and sunrise; the night.
Pertaining to nighttime; appropriate to the night.
Happening during the night.

nighttime.ety: From Middle English nyght tyme, nyȝttyme, equivalent to night + time. Compare Dutch nachttijd, German Nachtzeit, Danish nattetid, Swedish nattetid. Compare also Middle English nyȝter tyme (“nighttime”), from Old Norse náttartími, nætrtími (“nighttime”).

ex.en: It's already nighttime but the noise upstairs is horrible.
ex.ja: もう夜なのに上階の騒音が酷い。

ex.en: Even at nighttime, it was not quiet and peaceful any more.
ex.ja: もう夜になっても静かで平和ではありませんでした。

ex.en: If I eat this maybe it will sustain me until nighttime.
ex.ja: これ食べたら夜まで持つな。

note.ja: night（夜）+ time（時間）。「夜間」。

ex.ja: 彼は私より１０キロ体重が多い。

en: A bright green, biennial herb, Petroselinum crispum, having many cultivars.
The leaves of this plant used in Middle Eastern, European, and American cooking.
To add parsley to.

parsley.ety: From Middle English persely, from Old French peresil, from Latin petroselīnum, from Ancient Greek πετροσέλῑνον (petrosélīnon, “parsley”), from πέτρος (pétros, “rock, stone”) + σέλῑνον (sélīnon, “celery”). Displaced Old English petersiliġe, which goes back to the same root.

ex.en: Give me a bunch of parsley.
ex.ja: パセリを一束ください。

ex.en: Tom doesn't like parsley.
ex.ja: トムはパセリが嫌いなんだ。

ex.en: Maria doesn't like parsley.
ex.ja: マリアはパセリが苦手なのよ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 petroselinon（岩のパセリ）から。petra（岩）+ selinon（パセリ）。celery と同じ selinon。

en: A body suspended from a fixed support so that it swings freely back and forth under the influence of gravity, commonly used to regulate v…
The tendency of a situation to oscillate (between two extremes).

pendulum.ety: Borrowed from the neuter of Latin pendulus (“hanging”).

note.ja: ラテン語 pendulus（ぶら下がった）から。pendere（ぶら下がる）。「振り子」。pending と同じ。

en: A stake driven into the ground.
A type of punishment by which an offender had to rest his or her entire body weight on the top of a small stake.
To protest, organized by a labour union, typically in front of the location of employment.
To enclose or fortify with pickets or pointed stakes.

picket.ety: From French piquet, from piquer (“to pierce”).

note.ja: フランス語 piquet（とがった杭）から。piquer（突く）。「杭」→ 杭のように並んで見張る →「ピケ」。

en: Neat; eloquent; applicable; relevant.
Evoking strong mental sensation, to the point of distress; emotionally moving.

poignant.ety: From Middle English poynaunt, poynant, borrowed from Anglo-Norman puignant, poynaunt etc., present participle of poindre (“to prick”), from Latin pungō (“prick”). Doublet of pungent.

note.ja: 古フランス語 poindre（刺す）の現在分詞。ラテン語 pungere。「心を刺すような」→「痛切な」。pungent、point と同じ。

en: A person who has poliomyelitis.

ex.en: He was struck with polio when he was five.
ex.ja: 彼は五歳の時に小児麻痺にかかった。

ex.en: Africa is now polio-free.
ex.ja: 現在、アフリカにポリオはありません。

ex.en: She was vaccinated against polio.
ex.ja: ポリオワクチンは済んでいます。

en: Power, authority.
The ability or capacity to perform something

potency.ety: Borrowed from Latin potentia. Doublet of Potenza.

note.ja: pot（力がある）+ ency。力の強さ →「効力・影響力・勢力」。

en: Dangerously insecure or unstable; perilous.
Depending on the intention of another.

precarious.ety: From Latin precārius (“begged for, obtained by entreaty”), from prex, precis (“prayer”). Compare French précaire, Portuguese precário, and Spanish and Italian precario.

note.ja: ラテン語 precarius（祈って得た）から。prex（祈り）。「人の情けに頼る」→「不安定な」。pray と同じ。

en: A false, contrived, or assumed purpose or reason; a pretense.
To employ a pretext, which involves using a false or contrived purpose for soliciting the gain of something else.

pretext.ety: From Latin praetextum (“an ornament, etc., wrought in front, a pretense”), neuter of praetextus, past participle of praetexere (“to weave before, fringe or border, allege”).

ex.en: ... reason? What you're looking for is a pretext, isn't it?
ex.ja: ・・・理由？お前が欲しいのは口実だろ？

ex.en: He made up a pretext for a fight with me.
ex.ja: あいつに因縁を付けられた。

ex.en: He came to my house on the pretext of seeing me.
ex.ja: 彼は私に会うことを口実にして家に来た。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ text（織る）。前に織り出した表向きの理由 →「口実・言い訳」。

en: The transfer of a company or organization from government to private ownership and control.
The rendering of a thought or an idea, as private in scope.

privatization.ety: Calque of German Privatisierung (with English -ation), derived from Latin prīvātus (“apart from the state; private”), with reference to post-First World War German economic principles. Popularized by Sidney Merlin in 1943, who was aware of the term reprivatization (used in similar contexts), already attested at the time.

note.ja: priv（個人の）+ atization。個人（民間）のものにすること →「民営化」。

en: Pleasingly unusual; especially, having old-fashioned charm.

quaint.ety: From Middle English queynte, quoynte, from Anglo-Norman cointe, queinte and Old French cointe (“pretty, clever, knowing”), from Latin cognitus, past participle of cognōscō (“to know”).

ex.en: His accent sounds a little quaint.
ex.ja: 彼の口調は少しおかしい。

note.ja: 古フランス語 cointe（巧みな）から。ラテン語 cognitus（知られた）。「巧みな」→「古風で趣のある」。

en: An omnivorous, nocturnal mammal native to the Americas, of the genus Procyon, typically with a mixture of gray, brown, and black fur, a m…
The common raccoon (Procyon lotor).

raccoon.ety: From arocoun (1608), from Powhatan ärähkun, from ärähkuněm (“he scratches with his hands”).

ex.en: Raccoons are very smart.
ex.ja: アライグマは、すごく賢いんだよ。

ex.en: The raccoon drinks water.
ex.ja: アライグマは水を飲みます。

ex.en: There are raccoons at the zoo.
ex.ja: 動物園にアライグマがいる。

note.ja: アメリカ先住民ポーハタン語 aroughcun（手でひっかくもの）から。

en: The feeling of being reassured, of having confidence restored, of having apprehensions dispelled.
The act of confirming someone's opinion or impression.
The act of changing the distribution of resources.

en: To control or keep in check.
To deprive of liberty.

restrain.ety: From Middle English restreinen, from Old French restreindre, from Latin rēstringere (“fasten, tighten”).

ex.en: You should learn to restrain yourself.
ex.ja: 君は自分を抑えることを学ぶべきだ。

ex.en: He could no longer restrain himself.
ex.ja: 彼はもはや自分を抑制することができなかった。

ex.en: I told Jim to restrain himself from drinking too much.
ex.ja: 私はジムにあまり飲みすぎないようにと言った。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ stringere（締める）。「引き締める」→「抑える」。strict と同じ。

en: In an attractive or manner; full of colour or detail.
In a manner that occupies the non-visual senses; flavourfully, deeply.

richly.ety: Inherited from Middle English richely, from Old English rīċlīċe, from Proto-West Germanic *rīkīlīkō, from Proto-Germanic *rīkijalīkô; by surface analysis, rich + -ly (adverbial suffix).

ex.en: She is far from being richly gifted.
ex.ja: 彼女は才能に恵まれているどころではない。

ex.en: The queen was richly appareled.
ex.ja: 女王は豪華な服装をしていた。

ex.en: The room is richly ornamented.
ex.ja: その部屋は装飾を凝らしている。

note.ja: se（離れて）+ cess（行く）+ ion。離れて行くこと →「分離・脱退」。

Creative or having the power to originate.

Without worry or anxiety; unaffected by disturbance.
To make serene.
Serenity; clearness; calmness.

serene.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Latin serēnus (“clear, cloudless, untroubled”).

ex.en: The autumn sky is clear and serene.
ex.ja: 秋の空は澄み渡っている。

ex.en: The view of Mars through earthly telescopes suggested that all was serene.
ex.ja: 地上の望遠鏡で火星の様子を見ると、穏やかそのものだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 serenus（晴れた）から。「穏やかな」。serenity と同じ。

note.ja: ship（船）+ yard（作業場）。「造船所」。

en: Silicon dioxide.
Any of the silica group of the silicate minerals.

silica.ety: From New Latin silica, from Latin silex (“hard stone, flint”), on model of alumina, soda.

note.ja: ラテン語 silex（火打ち石）から。silicon と同じ。

en: To cook or undergo heating slowly at or below the boiling point.
To cause to cook or to cause to undergo heating slowly at or below the boiling point.
The state or process of simmering.

simmer.ety: From alteration of dialectal simper, from Middle English simperen (“to simmer”), of possibly imitative origin. First attested in the intransitive sense. The noun is from the verb. First attested in the late 15ᵗʰ century.

ex.en: What's the difference between boiling and simmering?
ex.ja: 茹でるのとぐつぐつ煮るのって何が違うの？

ex.en: Please simmer the beans for a while over a low heat.
ex.ja: とろ火で時間をかけて豆を炊いてください。

ex.en: Be sure to simmer on a low heat so it doesn't boil.
ex.ja: 必ず弱火で煮立たないように煮ること。

note.ja: 擬音語 simper から。「とろ火で煮る」→（怒りが）くすぶる。

en: A stump or base of a branch that has been lopped off; a short branch, or a sharp or rough branch.
A dead tree that remains standing.
To catch or tear (e.g. fabric) upon a rough surface or projection.
To damage or sink (a vessel) by collision; said of a tree or branch fixed to the bottom of a navigable body of water and partially submer…

snag.ety:
From earlier snag (“stump or branch of a tree”), from Middle English *snagge, *snage, from Old Norse snagi (“clothes peg”) (compare Old Norse snag-hyrndr (“snag-horned, having jagged corners”)), perhaps related to *sneganą, *snakaną (“to crawl, creep, wind about”) if the original meaning of the root *sneg- was more like “pointy object, stinging creature”. Note also *snakkōną (“to snap at, smack the lips; to blow”) (German schnacken (“to chat”)) and English sneck, snatch.
Compare Norwegian snag, snage (“protrusion; projecting point”), Icelandic snagi (“peg”). Also see the Dutch-origin fish name

note.ja: 北欧語に由来するとされる。「とがった突起」→ 引っかかる →「思わぬ障害」。

en: A cry with a short, sudden expulsion of breath.
The sound of sob.
To weep with convulsive gasps.
To say (something) while sobbing.

sob.ety: From Middle English sobben, perhaps from Middle Low German sabben (“to drool, slobber, salivate”). Cognate with West Frisian sabje, sobje (“to suck”), Dutch zabben, sabbelen (“to suck”), zabberen (“to drool”), German Low German sabbeln, severn (“to drool”), German sabbern (“to drool, slobber”), Norwegian sabbe (“to spill, drop, make a mess”). Compare also Old English sēofian (“to lament”), German saufen (“to drink, swig”).

ex.en: Between sobs, that lost girl said her name.
ex.ja: その迷子の女の子は泣きじゃくりながら名前を言った。

ex.en: The poor little girl did nothing but sob all day.
ex.ja: かわいそうにその少女は一日中泣いてばかりいた。

ex.en: The audience sobbed throughout the climax of the movie.
ex.ja: 観客は映画がクライマックスの間すすり泣きした。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。「すすり泣く」。

en: Enlightenment or education.
Cultivated intellectual worldliness; savoir-faire.

sophistication.ety: From Middle English sophisticacion, sophisticacioun, sophisticacoun, from Old French sofisticacion, sophisticacion, from Medieval Latin sophisticātiōnis. By surface analysis, sophisticate + -ion.

note.ja: sophisticate（洗練させる）+ -ion。ギリシャ語 sophistēs（知恵者）。「洗練」。sophisticated と同じ。

en: To cause to become straight.
To become straight.

straighten.ety: From straight + -en. Compare Scots strauchten (“to straighten”).

ex.en: I would like to have my teeth straightened.
ex.ja: 歯並びをきちんと直していただきたいのですが。

ex.en: I'd like to have her teeth straightened.
ex.ja: 娘の歯列を矯正していただきたいのです。

ex.en: I can't straighten out my back.
ex.ja: 腰が伸ばせません。

note.ja: straight（まっすぐな）+ -en。「まっすぐにする」。
